newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer urges tough stability pact for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer urges tough stability pact for EMU.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer on Tuesday said the European currency union needed a real deterrent against lax fiscal policies and urged policy-makers to adopt a tough stability pact.
"We need a real rule that acts as a deterrent against lax fiscal policies," Tietmeyer said in a speech prepared for delivery to a group of foreign bankers.

Tietmeyer said progress on the stability pact -- which will trigger automatic sanctions against nations who stray in fiscal austerity -- was good but warned the European Commission's proposal on the pact did not go far enough.

"I hope that it will be possible to approach the Dublin results and to clarify the still unresolved details," Tietmeyer said, adding that the Commission proposal was not as firm as he had expected following talks in Dublin in September.
Tietmeyer, one of the staunchest supporters of a strict interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty criteria, also warned, "In no event may the currency union become a transfer union."
